title: System font stacks and font pairing
when: The user wants to choose fonts, pair a heading font with a body font, or use fast system fonts with no downloads.
inputs: tone: modern, classic, friendly or technical
whether font files ship in the project folder
prompt:
Goal: Fonts that render instantly from the system or local files, one clear pairing, and safe fallbacks.
Steps:
1. Build stacks from CSS generic keywords: --font-sans: system-ui, sans-serif; --font-serif: ui-serif, serif; --font-mono: ui-monospace, monospace.
2. Pair by role: a serif heading over a sans body for a classic tone, one sans family in two weights for apps.
3. Keep to two families and three weights; mono only for code, and font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for aligned numbers.
4. If font files ship with the project, use @font-face with a relative woff2 url and font-display: swap, keeping the system stack as fallback.
5. Reduce swap shift with a fallback of similar x-height or a size-adjust in the @font-face.
6. Expose --font-body and --font-heading on :root and apply them on body and h1 to h3.
Quality bar:
- Text is readable before any custom font arrives.
- Heading and body fonts play clearly different roles.
- Never more than two families on screen.
Pitfalls:
- A remote font service, which needs the network.
- Script or display faces for body text.
- Faux bold from a missing weight file.
Verify:
- [ ] Each font-family ends with a generic keyword.
- [ ] Any @font-face uses a relative url and swap.
- [ ] At most two families.
- [ ] Code uses the mono stack.
Output: Font tokens and any @font-face rules at the top of style.css.

examples.input: which fonts should my law office site use
examples.output: headings ui-serif, serif at 600; body system-ui, sans-serif at 400; no downloads
